specMs.why: CLAUDE.md budget: process launch to first usable content, median of 10. Populated workspaces require the editable page frame; an empty workspace reports its index screen. pnpm perf:cold enforces 500 ms on Apple Silicon, while CI gates its separately measured hosted budget.

hostedCiMs.why: End-to-end budget on hosted macos-15. Three VMs of the same image measured series medians of 1449, 475, and 1634 ms with this harness, so the runner, not the app, sets the floor. 1.5 times the worst median, rounded up.

hostedNavToPaintMs.why: Navigation start to first content frame on hosted macos-15, the part the frontend controls. The same three VMs measured 242, 84, and 250 ms. 1.5 times the worst median, rounded up.

warmupRuns.why: The first launch of a fresh build pays signature checks and a cold page cache. Users see it once after brew upgrade, so it is logged and discarded.

timedRuns.why: SPEC: median of 10 runs. With an even count the median is the mean of the 5th and 6th sorted runs.

p95Ms.why: CLAUDE.md budget: key event to the first frame that shows the typed character, p95 in Playwright WebKit (EDIT-14).

hostedAppOwnedP95Ms.why: The app's share of key-to-paint on hosted macos-15: key event to the end of the input handler, plus the rendering update from its frame timestamp (the rAF callback argument, read before the first callback of the frame runs, so work the app queues in its own rAF counts) to the MessageChannel task after the recorder's rAF. One 60 Hz frame is 16 ms, so the app must finish its own work inside that. The tick wait in between is reported, not gated: the runner's first rendering update after input waits for its next 17 ms display tick, so three attempts of one job read tick-wait p95 18 ms and full key-to-paint p95 21 ms on the empty surface in every attempt while app-owned p95 read 4, 4, and 5 ms. The keystroke job gates this with AELOMI_PERF_CI=1. pnpm perf:keystroke gates p95Ms, the full key-to-paint, on Apple Silicon.

pageLoads.why: Three fresh page loads so one bad load cannot decide the verdict.

samplesPerLoad.why: 150 keys per load. With 15 discarded, 135 kept per load and 405 pooled for the p95.

discardedPerLoad.why: Frames right after a load are irregular. The first keys warm the page and are not counted.

gapMs.why: Keys 100 ms apart let the display link go idle between samples. Back-to-back keys measure vsync wait, not the app.

p95Ms.why: SPEC section 5: a query keystroke to the first frame showing current results over the 10,000-page mock fixture, one frame at 60 Hz.

hostedAppOwnedP95Ms.why: The hosted palette gate counts the same app-owned interval as the calibrated keystroke recorder. It retains the one-frame 16 ms threshold and reports full frame wait separately.

p95FrameMs.why: The 5,000-block page targets 60 Hz. WebKit reports whole-millisecond frame timestamps, so 16.7 ms rounds to 17 ms. This local gate does not include screencast tracing overhead.

maxFrameMs.why: SPEC editor fixture: no frame gap over 50 ms while scrolling the 5,000-block page. Both local and hosted modes enforce this maximum.

p95Ms.why: SPEC section 5: the complete Rust content query must stay below 5 ms p95 on the 10,000-page fixture. The release gate includes broad prefixes, common words, winner highlights, cold readers, both result limits and the additional 5,000-block page.

hostedP95Ms.why: Initially the same 5 ms budget as the product gate. Any future hosted-runner calibration must cite measured hosted runs; no multiplier or unmeasured allowance is used.

firstSamples.why: Thirty fresh-reader queries per bucket, with open, statement preparation and tokenizer creation inside the clock. The Rust gate also runs 200 steady queries and refuses fewer than 30 first-query samples.

maxLoadPerCore.why: 1-minute load average per CPU core above which a run is labelled NOISY. CI's quiet-machine wait releases below a load of 2.5 on the 3-core macos-15 runner, which is 0.83 per core, so 0.8 is the same bar rounded down. The label is information: it never changes a verdict or an exit code, and nothing waits for the load to fall.
